note: Slots chosen from 14-day Horizon /trade_aggregations medians for XLM/USDC, measured 2026-08-29. Hourly volume varies 4.5x across the day (180k XLM at 19:00 UTC to 818k at 14:00 UTC). Weekday medians: Thu 544k, Fri 495k, Sat 446k, Sun 362k, Wed 279k, Tue 249k, Mon 245k. The weekend is NOT the thin period on Stellar; Mon-Wed is.

slots.actual_note: Landed 2026-08-29T13:00:03Z, 60 min early, due to the launchd DST bug. Represents the 13:00 UTC hour (14d median 518,844 XLM), not the intended 14:00 peak.

slots.why: Thinnest hour of the week, weekend (re-dated from Sat after the run-2 network failure)
Thinnest hour on the thinnest day
Peak hour on a thin weekday
Peak hour on the thickest day
Insurance for the peak hour, which is still unsampled after run 1 drifted and run 6 was lost to sleep

corrections.what: launchd StartCalendarInterval fired one hour EARLY: 16:00 local was scheduled but the job ran at 13:00 UTC, i.e. 15:00 CEST. launchd applied standard time (CET, UTC+1) and ignored that the machine is on CEST (UTC+2).
corrections.effect: Run 1 landed at 13:00 UTC instead of 14:00 UTC. It is a valid measurement, just of the 13:00 UTC hour (14d median 518,844 XLM) rather than the intended peak hour (818,233). It is kept, not discarded; drift_minutes records the -60m.
corrections.fix: Scheduling moved out of launchd and into measure.mjs. The plist is now a 5-minute StartInterval poller and the slot decision is made in UTC epoch ms inside the script, where no timezone or DST can shift it.

corrections.what: Run 2 fired on wake at 18:05 UTC before the network interface was up. All 27 rows returned 'network: fetch failed', yet the empty file was still written and CLAIMED the slot.
corrections.effect: Slot 2 was silently burned. The file is quarantined at runs/failed/20260829T180532Z-run2-INCOMPLETE.jsonl and slot 2 is re-dated to 2026-08-30T19:00:00Z (Sun), which is a better thin-weekend sample anyway since Sunday is the quieter weekend day.
corrections.fix: measure.mjs now probes Horizon before starting and exits without writing if it is unreachable, and quarantines any run that fails a completeness check instead of letting it claim a slot.

corrections.what: Run 6 (Tue 14:00 UTC, the peak hour) never fired. The Mac was in deep sleep across the whole window; its periodic DarkWakes are 2 seconds and do not run LaunchAgents.
corrections.effect: The peak hour (14:00 UTC, 14d median 818,233 XLM) is still unsampled, because run 1 also missed it by an hour via the launchd DST bug. Run 8 is now the only planned chance at it.
corrections.fix: Slot 9 added on Fri 2026-09-04 14:00 UTC as insurance for the peak hour. Thursday is the thickest weekday (544k) and Friday the second thickest (495k), so slot 9 is the best available backup for slot 8.

corrections.what: The 3-hour catch-up window let a run claim a slot from a completely different hour. Run 4 landed +150m (07:30 UTC, 244k hour) against a planned 05:00 UTC (218k), and run 5 landed +160m (21:39 UTC, 393k hour) against a planned 19:00 UTC (180k).
corrections.effect: Run 5 was the expected worst case and did NOT measure the thin hour it was for. Runs 2 and 7 did land in the 19:00 UTC hour, so the thin end is still covered, but by accident of scheduling rather than by design.
corrections.fix: Catch-up window tightened from 3h to 45 min: a slot names an hour, so a run that cannot land in roughly that hour should leave the slot honestly PENDING rather than mislabel a different hour. Separately, report.mjs now labels every run by the hour it ACTUALLY measured and that hour's median volume, so the reader never has to trust the planned label.

script_versions.note: Original. launchd held the schedule; no preflight; an incomplete run could claim its slot.

Scheduling moved into the script in UTC after the launchd DST bug; added a Horizon preflight and quarantine of incomplete runs after run 2 burned its slot on a dead network. MEASUREMENT LOGIC IS UNCHANGED: same endpoint, pairs, sizes and both bps formulas, so runs across the two versions stay comparable.
Catch-up window tightened from 3h to 45 min so a late run cannot mislabel a different hour. MEASUREMENT LOGIC STILL UNCHANGED: same endpoint, pairs, sizes and both bps formulas.

hourly_median_source: Horizon /trade_aggregations, XLM/USDC, 336 hourly buckets, 2026-08-15 to 2026-08-29. Used to label each run by the hour it ACTUALLY measured, not the hour it was planned for.
